privacy.heading: today
lines: nothing is recorded. there is no endpoint to record to, no cookie
is set, and nothing is fetched from a third party. the typeface is
inlined in the page and the script is served from this domain, so
loading this screen tells nobody anything, including me.

privacy.heading: when command logging lands
lines: one thing will be recorded: a command typed at the shell that is
not a command. the string, and the day it was typed.
not the address it came from, not the user agent, not a cookie,
not a session id, not anything else. there is deliberately nothing
to join a record to, which is the whole design rather than a
promise about how carefully it will be handled.
the reason is small and honest. three people typing blog is the
cheapest research available about what to build next.

privacy.heading: when telemetry lands
lines: the numbers will come from one machine, pushed out by it on a fixed
cadence. nothing reaches in to ask.
they are bucketed rather than instantaneous, and derived rather
than read: no hostname, no kernel, no address, no paths. a steady
stream of precise values would publish a sleep schedule, which is
worth more to a stranger than any of it is to you.

privacy.heading: the design
lines: the terminal, the agent and everything drawn here are original.
the grammar is borrowed from the tools this trade runs on. the
marks are borrowed from nobody.
